risks.occurred: Yes. On 12 Oct the client asked for AI-detection research.
risks.mitigation_used: Formal change request assessing 150 to 250 extra hours; the team proposed a conceptual AI-use monitoring framework instead, which the client approved; three Jira tasks added under epics 9 and 10.
risks.outcome: Scope kept manageable; the alternative became a central recommendation (D3 Part C).

risks.occurred: Yes. 96 logged records plus 494 from the update search.
risks.mitigation_used: Clear criteria, dual AI-assisted screening with adjudication, and proportionate extraction for non-computing studies.
risks.outcome: 586 records screened in about two days; agreement kappa 0.80 to 0.88.

risks.occurred: Yes. 33 of 143 included studies are computing-specific, and the core computing studies average 2.7/5 for quality.
risks.mitigation_used: Computing studies prioritised (Core tier); evidence from other fields used as transferable support; confidence ratings lowered where computing evidence was thin.

risks.occurred: Partly. The Excel evidence log lagged behind Covidence, and the screening focus was sharpened mid-review (Amendment 3, redesign focus).
risks.mitigation_used: Written protocols, two blinded screeners, a dated protocol amendment applied to all records, and calibration rules for D2.
risks.outcome: Measured agreement and a full audit trail.

risks.occurred: Avoided. CS1QA (2022) was screened out as pre-GenAI.
risks.mitigation_used: Data quality and relevance checked before analysis (method decision M6).
risks.outcome: Three datasets kept, each with known limits.

risks.occurred: Partly. StudyChat was added as a third dataset, and two team analyses covered the same datasets.
risks.mitigation_used: Analyses limited to the research questions.
risks.outcome: The duplication became an independent replication (key figures matched exactly).

risks.occurred: Yes. Most capability data use 2023 models, and new 2026 studies appeared.
risks.mitigation_used: One targeted update search (as planned), a cut-off date of 16 Oct 2026, and a currency rule excluding pre-GenAI evidence.
risks.outcome: Evidence current to Oct 2026; model age stated as a limitation.

risks.occurred: No. Team availability was consistent throughout.
risks.mitigation_used: Shared records in OneDrive and Jira; backup responsibilities

risks.occurred: Yes. No included computing redesign study had a control group.
risks.mitigation_used: Every recommendation is linked to evidence and carries an evidence status (Implemented / Proposal).
risks.outcome: 8 of 15 decision-guide cells are labelled proposals.

lessons: Keep one source of truth. Screening was done in Covidence, but the Excel evidence log lagged about three weeks behind it, so the two records disagreed until 17 Oct. Export Covidence decisions to the log weekly.
Record search strings and dates at the time of searching. Their absence cost a full update search later and remains a PRISMA limitation.

The sequential, waterfall-like literature stream (protocol, then search, then screening, then extraction) left synthesis compressed into Wk 11. Running dataset analysis in parallel from Wk 6 would have reduced the late load.
A formal change request protected the schedule and produced a better deliverable than simply accepting or refusing the client's request.
Duplicate analyses are wasteful unless planned. Here they turned into a useful replication, but splitting work explicitly would have saved effort.
effort_changes: More than planned: screening and selection. An unplanned, documented OpenAlex update search added 494 records to screen, and a protocol amendment (redesign focus) was applied to all records.

More than planned: scope-change work. Three tasks (AI-use monitoring research, conceptual framework, integration into D3) were added under epics 9 and 10, 60 hours approved and logged separately, against the change request's estimate of 150 to 250 hours if detection had been added in full.

More than planned: dataset analysis. The three datasets were analysed independently twice, which doubled effort but gave a replication check (StudyChat and Hannover figures matched; EPFL agreed in direction).
Less than planned or redistributed: AI-assisted screening, extraction and drafting (budgeted as AI productivity tools) reduced the manual hours for screening and synthesis.
As planned: proposal, protocol, synthesis timing and the mid-semester break.

scope_change_agreement: Client requested AI detection; team estimated 150-250 hours (A$9,750-16,250 at A$65/h). Agreed middle ground: a system that identifies AI use in unsupervised assessments from recorded evidence, rather than a text detector (the AI-use monitoring framework). +60 hours (A$3,900), logged separately: Sachin 20, Prajwal 20, Nadia 10, Anshul 10. Approved by the client and the mentor; delivered within the original timeline.
